PullRequest.Title: Reuse text buffers in chat edits for checkpoint replay
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Addresses the renderer-freeze portion of #296064. Checkpoint reconstruction currently rebuilds a text buffer from the entire file for every recorded text edit operation, repeatedly scanning and copying the same content on the renderer thread.

- Reuse one buffer across consecutive ordinary-text edit operations, applying each batch in order rather than flattening ranges from different document versions.
- Stop batching at file lifecycle boundaries and leave notebook replay on its existing path.
- Preserve the existing inter-batch BOM and default-EOL normalization, and dispose the buffer when replay succeeds or throws.
- Add deterministic buffer-creation/disposal regressions and coverage for dependent ranges, LF/CRLF, UTF-16, no-op reconstruction, concurrent snapshots, errors, and file recreation.

No public API, persistence-format, configuration, or UI changes. This does not claim to resolve the separately reported incomplete-file-restoration behavior, which was not reproduced.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client` — zero errors.
- Targeted `node build/hygiene.ts` on both changed files — passed.
- 98 tests passed across checkpoint timeline, chat editing actions, editing service, and modified notebook entry suites using `scripts/test.bat`.
- Confirmed the buffer-reuse and error-cleanup regression tests fail on the original implementation and pass with this change.
- Three recorded runs of the actual production implementation in isolated Code OSS on Windows x64, without replay monkeypatching. Synthetic workload: 2,000 edit operations over a 20,000-line, 1.62 MB file.

| Measurement | Before | After (3 runs) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Undo completion | 10.90–10.92 s | 53.8 / 38.8 / 35.8 ms |
| Zero-delay renderer timer | 10.85–10.89 s | 26.6 / 21.0 / 19.3 ms |

Verified the restored file SHA-256 matches the baseline exactly, and checked snapshot reads, redo, and subsequent checkpoint restore against the expected file contents.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Checkpoint replay rebuilt and reserialized the entire text buffer for every recorded text-edit operation, producing O(K*N)-style full-document CPU/allocation work for K small batches over a large file and blocking undo, redo, restore, and cold snapshot/diff model creation.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Large chat-edited files with many recorded edit operations can freeze or substantially delay checkpoint undo/redo/restore and cold historical diff rendering because repeated full-document scans and copies execute before those actions complete.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added contiguous TextEdit grouping applies all version-ordered edit batches to one PieceTreeTextBuffer and extracts content only once per ordinary-text run, reducing full-buffer construction/extraction from one per edit operation to one per run while retaining create/delete/rename and notebook boundaries and disposing the buffer in finally.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, _replayOperations awaited _applyOperationToState once for every TextEdit operation; that branch called _applyTextEditsToContent for each operation. _applyTextEditsToContent calls createTextBuffer on the complete current content, whose createTextBufferFactory passes the entire string to PieceTreeTextBufferBuilder.acceptChunk/createLineStarts, and then extracts the complete resulting string. The path is directly awaited by undoInteraction/redoInteraction/restoreSnapshot through navigateToCheckpoint, and by snapshot-model creation used for diff rendering. Thus K edit batches over a document of size N repeatedly scan and materialize the full document on the renderer-side critical path. The PR's tests also establish the old multiplicity versus the fixed invariant by asserting one buffer creation/disposal for multiple edit operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Undo, redo, or explicit restore of a chat editing checkpoint containing many ordinary-text edit batches across one or more files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user action awaits undoInteraction/redoInteraction/restoreSnapshot, then navigateToCheckpoint, sequential filesystem lifecycle operations, reconstruction of every affected file, and setContents for each surviving file. The changed grouping is directly on this critical path and reduces synchronous CPU/allocation before setContents can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply create, delete, and rename lifecycle edits through the bulk edit delegate
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One boundary call per lifecycle operation crossed between the current and target epochs, serialized in epoch order; text edit operations add no lifecycle boundary call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical serialized per-lifecycle-operation calls occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All lifecycle calls complete before content reconstruction starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write reconstructed contents into each surviving affected document via the session delegate
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one setContents call per distinct affected surviving resource after ResourceSet deduplication, launched across resources with Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-write-per-deduplicated-surviving-resource behavior existed; only the number of temporary text-buffer reconstructions before the write is reduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action waits for all writes; the changed CPU replay finishes before each file's write.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Affected file count F; for each file, document length N, recorded text-edit batch count K, and contiguous ordinary-text runs R after create/delete/rename boundaries. Before the PR full-buffer construction/extraction scaled approximately with K*N; after it scales with R*N plus the edits themselves, where R is normally 1 and at most K.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Create/delete/rename operations are awaited serially in epoch order. Affected-file reconstructions and subsequent setContents calls are launched with Promise.all across files; each file's text-buffer edit replay is synchronous and isolated. The diff does not increase aggregate file concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Checkpoint restoration does not cache reconstructed strings; repeated navigations reconstruct again both before and after the PR. The optimization is per invocation and has no stale/negative cache behavior. Each contiguous run owns and disposes one temporary buffer in finally.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed loop groups consecutive TextEdit operations, createTextBuffer scans the full string, output extraction materializes the full result, and the user action awaits this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on file sizes, edit history, and affected-file count, but the old full-document work per edit and the new one-buffer-per-run behavior are directly established. PR-provided timings indicate a large real symptom but are not needed to establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. This is a concrete repeated-work fix: it lowers full-document scans/copies from K to R without adding boundary calls, concurrency, or retained buffers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and warm historical snapshot/diff model creation for chat-edited files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold model request, the snapshot content provider calls getSnapshotModel/getContentAtStop, which reconstructs the requested historical content before creating the text model. Diff observables request original and modified snapshot models in parallel, then await editor-worker diff computation. Warm existing models and finalized diff-cache entries bypass reconstruction or computation. The changed replay is on the cold critical path only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the original/modified text diff in the editor worker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker request per uncached observed diff key after the two snapshot models are ready; active identical keys coalesce and finalized keys cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor-worker call cardinality, cache keys, and scheduling existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Diff UI remains busy until the worker result; the changed replay only reduces prerequisite local CPU before this unchanged request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Observed file diffs D, usually two historical models per uncached diff; per snapshot, document length N and text-edit batches K between baseline and target. Grouping reduces reconstruction from K full-buffer rebuilds to one per contiguous ordinary-text run. Effective cardinality is per distinct uncached snapshot URI/diff key, not per UI row after model/cache reuse.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two snapshot model references for one diff use Promise.all. Multiple observed per-file diffs may progress concurrently. _refCountedDiffs coalesces the same active key and _finalizedDiffCache serves completed final keys. The diff does not change concurrency or coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The model service returns an existing live snapshot model on warm access. Active identical diff requests share _refCountedDiffs, and finalized diffs use _finalizedDiffCache. Cold misses reconstruct; failed provider/model requests are not newly cached by this diff. Grouping is local to each miss.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider, model-cache, ref-count, finalized-cache, and editor-worker paths are explicit, and no changed line alters their scheduling or keying.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously observed file diffs and model-cache hit rate vary by UI surface. The reduction in prerequisite replay work is certain; exact user-visible gain varies with N and K.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Cold reconstruction becomes cheaper, while warm cache behavior, active coalescing, worker IPC cardinality, and concurrency are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live snapshot model refreshes while agent edits continue
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Operation changes schedule getContentAtStop through a 500 ms ThrottledDelayer; reconstruction completes before the callback replaces the snapshot model value. The changed replay runs on each executed refresh, but reduces rather than increases full-buffer work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Recorded edit history up to the target epoch K, current document length N, and operation-event frequency. Coalescing limits execution to approximately one refresh per 500 ms burst; finalization disposes the listener after the target epoch is reached.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One ThrottledDelayer per live snapshot subscription coalesces operation events. Separate snapshot subscriptions can refresh independently; this behavior is unchanged. Each reconstruction owns a separate temporary buffer, as covered by concurrent reconstruction tests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No reconstructed-content cache is used for live targets because content changes. Event bursts are time-coalesced, and the subscription disposes when finalized. The diff does not alter keys, negative caching, or subscription lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the 500 ms scheduler, reconstruction call, callback, and changed one-buffer-per-run replay are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously open live snapshots varies, but event throttling and per-call isolation are established. Exact model setValue cost depends on document size and is unchanged downstream work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Refresh frequency and downstream model replacement are unchanged; each refresh performs fewer full-document allocations/scans and disposes its buffer.

Scenarios.Scenario: Notebook checkpoint reconstruction, including cell text edits and final notebook snapshot serialization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Notebook baselines create an untitled notebook model, replay notebook/cell operations in order, resolve the notebook data provider, serialize the final snapshot, and dispose the notebook model. The new ordinary-text grouping is gated off whenever currentState.notebook exists; the only notebook change wraps the existing single edit batch in an outer array.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/activate the notebook data provider before serializing the reconstructed notebook snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per surviving notebook reconstruction after all operations; separate notebooks follow the pre-existing per-resource Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider resolution, notebook serialization, model lifecycle, and per-notebook cardinality existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notebook reconstruction waits for provider resolution and serialization before returning content.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Notebook cell count, notebook operation count, and edited-cell content sizes. Cell text edits still create one temporary text buffer per cell TextEdit operation, exactly as before; notebook serialization remains once per surviving reconstructed notebook.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations within one notebook replay remain sequential. Separate affected notebooks may reconstruct under the existing Promise.all across resources. The diff does not add notebook parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new notebook cache is added. Provider resolution and snapshot serialization follow the prior path. Temporary cell buffers and the notebook model retain their existing disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the !currentState.notebook guard and unchanged provider/serialization path are explicit; the signature adaptation supplies one group for the existing cell behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider activation cost and notebook sizes vary, but the changed grouping is provably excluded from notebook state and does not alter this boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Notebook replay cost, boundary count, concurrency, and cleanup remain unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and the performance-relevant call graph. The PR fixes repeated full-document text-buffer reconstruction on checkpoint and cold snapshot replay, preserves lifecycle and notebook boundaries, disposes temporary buffers on success and failure, and does not increase filesystem/IPC fan-out, concurrency, cache retention, or live-refresh frequency. No reportable performance findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
